blocking.section: Import tool fidelity levels / Levels and guarantees; Concept mapping / Worked import example
blocking.issue: The `exact` and `equivalent` guarantees contradict the sourced KrakenD default that the document states itself. The research says that with `input_headers` and `input_query_strings` absent (default `[]`), KrakenD forwards no client headers or query strings. Ruralz forwards them all. Every imported Route therefore sends different bytes to its Upstreams, including `Authorization` and cookies. The worked example has no `input_headers`, yet it grades its Upstreams `equivalent`, reports 'manual 0' and exits 0. That is a security-relevant difference, and the report shows no item for it.
blocking.evidence: Line 453: '`exact` | For every request, the generated configuration yields the same routing, the same decision and the same bytes on the wire as the KrakenD setting did'. Line 140: 'KrakenD forwards nothing by default; Ruralz forwards client headers and query strings unless a Policy removes them'. Line 859: 'Nothing forwarded unless allowlisted ([source](https://www.krakend.io/schema/v2.13/krakend.json))'. Lines 434 and 442: 'items: exact 4, equivalent 13, approximate 3, manual 0' and 'exit status 0 (no manual items)'. krakend-config-model.md section 3: '`input_headers` | array, `[]` | Case-insensitive allowlist. No client headers are forwarded by default'.
blocking.fix: Emit one security-flagged report item per Route for the forwarding default, whether or not `input_headers` or `input_query_strings` is present: `manual` under OQ-migration-from-krakend-7 option (a) until OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-5 closes. Update the worked example to show that item, the new counts ('manual 1'), exit status 1 and the Route annotation `manual`. blocking.section: Concept mapping / extra_config namespaces (qos/ratelimit/router); Worked import example; Cutover runbook / Stage 5; Migration gaps / Behavior changes to plan for
blocking.issue: The document says without condition that Ruralz enforces imported limits once across the whole Cluster. Foundation pack sections 2 and 8.8 and the Configuration model make that true only with the `redis` driver. With no Gateway `stateStore` and no `RURALZ_STATE_STORE_URL`, the driver is `memory` and every limit multiplies by the Node count. The worked example emits a `ratelimit` Policy and no `stateStore`, and the report text then states a false Cluster-wide limit. Its advice to 'multiply by the KrakenD instance count' would inflate capacity a second time on `memory`. Stage 0 step 4 states the correct rule, so the document contradicts itself.
blocking.evidence: Line 190: 'Ruralz enforces one Cluster-wide limit ([OQ-migration-from-krakend-12](#open-questions))'. Lines 438 and 439: 'Ruralz enforces 50 per 1s across the Cluster; multiply by the KrakenD instance count to keep capacity'. Line 857: 'One Cluster-wide limit through the State Store'. Line 749: 'KrakenD per instance and Ruralz Cluster-wide'. The worked-example Gateway (lines 326 to 341) has no `stateStore`. Line 706: 'the `memory` driver multiplies every limit by the Node count'. Pack 8.8: 'With the `memory` driver every limit multiplies by the Node count'. Configuration model Gateway: 'Without `stateStore`, `ruralzd` reads `RURALZ_STATE_STORE_URL`, else uses `memory` ... because `memory` multiplies every Rate Limit and Quota by the Node count'.
blocking.fix: Add an importer rule: when the output contains any `ratelimit`, `quota` or `cache` Policy, emit Gateway `stateStore: {driver: redis, url: {secretRef: {provider: env, name: RURALZ_STATE_STORE_URL}}}` and list the secret to provision. blocking.section: Cutover runbook / Stage 4 shadow traffic; Rollback
blocking.issue: The shadow exit gate and a rollback trigger apply SM-4 outside the scenario that SM-4 defines. The Vision defines SM-4 for one reference scenario: JWT and a local token bucket, no Plugins or State Store Policy, at half of saturation RPS, excluding Upstream and State Store time. Migrated production traffic includes State Store rate limits, quotas, caches and ported Plugins. The Vision tags a same-zone State Store round trip alone at up to 1 ms p99 (hypothesis). So 'as SM-4 defines' misstates the cited metric, and the 1 ms trigger would roll back healthy cutovers.

blocking.section: Concept mapping / extra_config namespaces (auth/api-keys S with auth/validator E); Import tool fidelity levels / Rules that hold at every level
blocking.issue: The `equivalent` grade for service-scope `auth/api-keys` contradicts foundation pack 8.12 and the document's own rule 2. All client authentication types share slot `auth`, so a Route `auth.jwt` imported from endpoint-scope `auth/validator` replaces the Gateway `auth.api-key`. An endpoint that KrakenD protected with both an API key and a JWT therefore loses its API-key check, and the report records no item. The document never cites OQ-configuration-model-13, which owns how one Route accepts or combines two client authentication types.

Pack 8.12 step 2: 'A Route Policy in the same `slot` as a remaining Gateway Policy replaces it (Route over Gateway) ... All client authentication types share slot `auth`'. Configuration model Policy: 'How one Route accepts either JWT or an API key in the single `auth` slot is OQ-configuration-model-13.'
